label: Nobleman
summary: Another name of the game concept Noble, as "Nobleman": a character who belongs to a dynasty.
details: In a text, `[nobleman|E]` shows the word "Nobleman" linked to the Noble explanation. No vanilla text uses this name.

label: Noblemen
summary: Another name of the game concept Noble, as "Noblemen": characters who belong to a dynasty.
details: In a text, `[noblemen|E]` shows the word "Noblemen" linked to the Noble explanation. No vanilla text uses this name.

label: Nobles
summary: Another name of the game concept Noble, in the plural: characters who belong to a dynasty.
details: In a text, `[nobles|E]` shows the word "Nobles" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in concept texts, for example that captured nobles go into house arrest.

label: Noblewoman
summary: Another name of the game concept Noble, as "Noblewoman": a character who belongs to a dynasty.
details: In a text, `[noblewoman|E]` shows the word "Noblewoman" linked to the Noble explanation. The vanilla lines found write `noblewoman.GetFirstName`, where `noblewoman` is a saved scope of an event, not this concept.

label: Noblewomen
summary: Another name of the game concept Noble, as "Noblewomen": characters who belong to a dynasty.
details: In a text, `[noblewomen|E]` shows the word "Noblewomen" linked to the Noble explanation. No vanilla text uses this name.

label: Nomad
summary: Another name of the game concept Nomadic, as "Nomad": a nomadic ruler, who grazes county fertility to grow a herd.
details: In a text, `[nomad|E]` shows the word "Nomad" linked to the concept's explanation. Nomads use their herd as a horde that can be upgraded to men-at-arms, live in a yurt, can migrate to more fertile land and have a higher maximum dread. Vanilla uses it in court position and decision texts.

label: Nomad icon
summary: The icon of the game concept Nomadic (the nomad government of herding rulers).
details: In a text, `[nomad_i|E]` shows the nomad government icon linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in front of the word in modifier texts, and without `|E` for just the icon.

label: Nomadic
summary: The game concept Nomadic: rulers who graze county fertility to grow their herd and can migrate to more fertile lands.
details: In a text, `[nomadic|E]` shows the word "Nomadic" linked to the concept's explanation. Their herd serves as a horde that can be upgraded to men-at-arms; big nomadic realms also grow their herd through tributaries or a high fertility equilibrium. Nomads have a higher maximum dread.

label: Dominance
summary: The game concept Dominance: the power a nomadic ruler projects, which grows with the size of their herd and unlocks more migration options.
details: In a text, `[nomadic_authority|E]` shows the word "Dominance" linked to the concept's explanation. It has five levels, from unruly to unrestricted; only one ruler per playthrough can ever reach the last. Vanilla uses it in government and migration interaction texts.

label: Nomadic government
summary: Another name of the game concept Nomadic, as "Nomadic Government": the government of herding rulers who graze county fertility and can migrate.
details: In a text, `[nomadic_government|E]` shows the words "Nomadic Government" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in innovation texts (nomadic rulers can only use tribal era innovations).

label: Nomadic settlement
summary: The game concept Nomadic Settlement: the holding type of nomadic rulers, standing for a yurt on the map.
details: In a text, `[nomadic_holding|E]` shows the words "Nomadic Settlement" linked to the concept's explanation. It gives a little county control and county opinion. Vanilla uses it in the texts for razing a holding and replacing it with a nomadic one, which is better for county fertility.

label: Nomadic settlements
summary: Another name of the game concept Nomadic Settlement, in the plural: the holdings of nomadic rulers, each a yurt on the map.
details: In a text, `[nomadic_holdings|E]` shows the concept's name linked to its explanation; the English text for this plural is also "Nomadic Settlement". Vanilla uses it in decision and raze texts.

label: Nomads
summary: Another name of the game concept Nomadic, in the plural "Nomads": rulers who graze county fertility to grow a herd and can migrate.
details: In a text, `[nomads|E]` shows the word "Nomads" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in the dread and vassal stance texts.

label: Nominal duumvirate
summary: The game concept Nominal Duumvirate: an empire ruled by a senior emperor and a junior emperor who is still a child.
details: In a text, `[nominal_duumvirate|E]` shows the words "Nominal Duumvirate" linked to the concept's explanation. A duumvirate is the rule of one empire by two characters; the nominal one becomes a full duumvirate when the junior emperor comes of age. Junior emperors give passive influence to themselves and the senior emperor.

label: Nominal duumvirates
summary: Another name of the game concept Nominal Duumvirate, in the plural: empires ruled by a senior emperor and a child junior emperor.
details: In a text, `[nominal_duumvirates|E]` shows the words "Nominal Duumvirates" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in the list of diarchy types and as the name of a cultural tradition's unlock.

label: Nominate
summary: The game concept Nominate: under elective succession laws, each elector names the heir they prefer for the title.
details: In a text, `[nominate|E]` shows the word "Nominate" linked to the concept's explanation. Who can be a candidate and how electors choose depends on the law. No vanilla text uses this name.

label: Nominate heir
summary: Another name of the game concept Nominate, as "Nominate Heir": an elector naming the heir they prefer under an elective succession law.
details: In a text, `[nominate_heir|E]` shows the words "Nominate Heir" linked to the concept's explanation. No vanilla text uses this name.

label: Nomination
summary: Another name of the game concept Nominate, as "Nomination": an elector's choice of preferred heir under an elective succession law.
details: In a text, `[nomination|E]` shows the word "Nomination" linked to the concept's explanation. No vanilla text uses this name.

label: Nominations
summary: Another name of the game concept Nominate, in the plural "Nominations": the electors' choices of preferred heir under an elective succession law.
details: In a text, `[nominations|E]` shows the word "Nominations" linked to the concept's explanation. No vanilla text uses this name.

label: Oath
summary: The game concept Oath: a vow the host swears during a coronation, which helps a new ruler secure legitimacy.
details: In a text, `[oath|E]` shows the word "Oath" linked to the concept's explanation. Oaths unlock time-limited decisions the ruler must complete to prove worthy of the title; the coronation's magnificence affects the rewards. Vanilla uses it in building texts about fulfilled oaths.

label: Oaths
summary: Another name of the game concept Oath, in the plural: vows sworn during a coronation that help a new ruler secure legitimacy.
details: In a text, `[oaths|E]` shows the word "Oaths" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in coronation activity texts.

label: Obedience
summary: The game concept Obedience: in nomadic realms, the loyalty of a character to their liege, suzerain or the owner of their court.
details: In a text, `[obedience|E]` shows the word "Obedience" linked to the concept's explanation. A character can be obedient to only one ruler. Obedient characters are less likely to scheme, go to war or join factions against their liege, back the liege's succession choices and do not press claims on them.

label: Obedience icon
summary: The icon of the game concept Obedience (a character's loyalty to a nomadic ruler).
details: In a text, `[obedience_i|E]` shows the obedience icon linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla writes it without `|E` (`[obedience_i]`) to put the icon in effect and court position texts.

label: Obedience threshold
summary: The game concept Obedience Threshold: the score a character must reach to count as obedient.
details: In a text, `[obedience_threshold|E]` shows the words "Obedience Threshold" linked to the concept's explanation. The threshold depends on close family ties to the overlord, being primary heir, friendship or rivalry, traits and employment in the kurultai or court; children are more likely to be obedient than adults.

label: Obedient
summary: Another name of the game concept Obedience, as "Obedient": a character loyal to a nomadic ruler.
details: In a text, `[obedient|E]` shows the word "Obedient" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in effect texts ("Becomes obedient to X").

label: Objectives
summary: The game concept Objectives: the parts of an enemy realm whose occupation makes war score tick up over time, usually the capital and holdings in the war target's area.
details: In a text, `[objectives|E]` shows the word "Objectives" linked to the concept's explanation. For the defender, war score starts ticking after a while if the attackers occupy no objectives. Vanilla uses it in the war overview and declare war texts.

label: Obligation
summary: Another name of the game concept Subject Obligations, in the singular: how much tax and how many levies a subject owes their suzerain.
details: In a text, `[obligation|E]` shows the word "Obligation" linked to the concept's explanation. The subject's government form decides how the obligations are set, for example through the vassal contract for feudal and clan vassals. Vanilla uses it in vassal contract effect texts.

label: Obligations
summary: Another name of the game concept Subject Obligations, in the plural: how much tax and how many levies a subject owes their suzerain.
details: In a text, `[obligations|E]` shows the word "Obligations" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it often in vassal and government texts.

label: Occupation
summary: The game concept Occupation: a holding taken over for the time being by a hostile ruler during a war, after a successful siege.
details: In a text, `[occupation|E]` shows the word "Occupation" linked to the concept's explanation. An army besieges a hostile fortified holding when it outnumbers the garrison; occupying it gives war score but does not make it yours, only the war target's land can change hands. Vanilla uses it in a rally point text.

label: Occupations
summary: Another name of the game concept Occupation, in the plural: holdings held for the time being by a hostile ruler during a war.
details: In a text, `[occupations|E]` shows the word "Occupations" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in effect and travel danger texts.

label: Occupied
summary: Another name of the game concept Occupation, as "Occupied": a holding held for the time being by a hostile ruler during a war.
details: In a text, `[occupied|E]` shows the word "Occupied" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in effect and siege texts.

label: Occupies
summary: Another name of the game concept Occupation, as the verb "Occupies": an army taking a hostile holding after a siege.
details: In a text, `[occupies|E]` shows the word "Occupies" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in an accolade text.

label: Occupy
summary: Another name of the game concept Occupation, as the verb "Occupy": to take a hostile holding for the time being during a war.
details: In a text, `[occupy|E]` shows the word "Occupy" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in concept texts on armies and fortified holdings.

label: Occupying
summary: Another name of the game concept Occupation, as "Occupying": taking hostile holdings for the time being during a war.
details: In a text, `[occupying|E]` shows the word "Occupying" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in the war and war score concept texts.

label: Offensive war opinion
summary: The game concept Offensive War Opinion: the growing dislike vassals feel for a liege who is the main attacker in a war.
details: In a text, `[offensive_war_opinion|E]` shows the words "Offensive War Opinion" linked to the concept's explanation. It starts after a grace period in months (a game define) and slowly fades once the war is over; civil wars and great holy wars do not count. Vanilla uses it in AI personality texts.

label: Offensive war (short)
summary: Another name of the game concept Offensive War Opinion, in a short form: vassals' dislike of a liege who is the main attacker in a war.
details: In a text, `[offensive_war_opinion_short|E]` shows the words "Offensive War" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it as the name of that opinion in the character relations texts.

label: Offer vassalization
summary: The game concept Offer Vassalization: an interaction that offers an independent ruler of lower title rank to become your vassal, adding them to the realm peacefully.
details: In a text, `[offer_vassalization|E]` shows the words "Offer Vassalization" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in texts that raise its acceptance.

label: Offer vassalization interaction
summary: Another name of the game concept Offer Vassalization: the interaction that offers an independent ruler of lower rank to become your vassal.
details: In a text, `[offer_vassalization_interaction|E]` shows the words "Offer Vassalization Interaction" linked to the concept's explanation. No vanilla text uses this name.

label: Officer
summary: The game concept Officer: a special role a follower can be given to help their camp.
details: In a text, `[officer|E]` shows the word "Officer" linked to the concept's explanation. Officers work much like court positions, with benefits based on the holder's aptitude, but appointing them is free and they draw no salary; revoking one still costs prestige. Vanilla uses it often in court position texts.

label: Officers
summary: Another name of the game concept Officer, in the plural: special roles followers can be given to help their camp.
details: In a text, `[officers|E]` shows the word "Officers" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in the camp texts.

label: Opinion
summary: The game concept Opinion: what one character thinks of another, a one-way value from -100 to +100.
details: In a text, `[opinion|E]` shows the word "Opinion" linked to the concept's explanation. Every character has an opinion of every other one, and it drives how they behave towards them. Vanilla uses it in hundreds of texts.

label: Opinion icon
summary: The icon of the game concept Opinion (what one character thinks of another).
details: In a text, `[opinion_i|E]` shows the opinion icon linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla mostly writes it without `|E` (`[opinion_i]`) to put the icon before a number.

label: Opinions
summary: Another name of the game concept Opinion, in the plural: what characters think of each other, each from -100 to +100.
details: In a text, `[opinions|E]` shows the word "Opinions" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in concept texts on the domain limit and culture.

label: Organize army
summary: The game concept Organize Army: a council task of the marshal that raises garrison size and levy reinforcement rate in the liege's realm.
details: In a text, `[organize_levies|E]` shows the task's name ("Organize Army") linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in a list of council tasks.

label: Organized faith
summary: The game concept Organized: a faith with a religious hierarchy, organized worship and formal scriptures.
details: In a text, `[organized|E]` shows the word "Organized" linked to the concept's explanation. Unreformed pagan faiths become organized by reforming; all other faiths always count as organized. Vanilla uses it in the texts on creating empires, which can require an organized faith.

label: Overlord
summary: The game concept Overlord: a ruler to whom another ruler has sworn loyalty as a vassal or a tributary.
details: In a text, `[overlord|E]` shows the word "Overlord" linked to the concept's explanation. Both suzerains and lieges count as overlords. Vanilla uses it in war and realm texts.

label: Overlord's (possessive)
summary: Another name of the game concept Overlord, in the possessive form: a ruler to whom another has sworn loyalty as vassal or tributary.
details: In a text, `[overlord_possessive|E]` shows the word "Overlord's" linked to the concept's explanation. No vanilla text uses this name.

label: Owned legend
summary: The game concept Owned Legend: a legend owned by a ruler, who gets most of its effects.
details: In a text, `[owned_legend|E]` shows the words "Owned Legend" linked to the concept's explanation. The owner can be the legend's protagonist but need not be; promoters can pay a monthly sum to get part of its bonuses. Vanilla uses it as the name of the legend's expenses.

label: Owning legend
summary: Another name of the game concept Owned Legend, as "Owning Legend": a legend owned by a ruler, who gets most of its effects.
details: In a text, `[owning_legend|E]` shows the words "Owning Legend" linked to the concept's explanation. No vanilla text uses this name.

label: Paiza
summary: The game concept Paiza: a small metal tablet (also called a gerege) issued by a powerful steppe ruler, which carries the khan's authority.
details: In a text, `[paiza|E]` shows the word "Paiza" linked to the concept's explanation. In the game they are artifacts that a powerful nomadic ruler gives to favorites through the grant paiza interaction; a decision sets up the paiza system and opens further decisions. Vanilla uses it in an obedience reason text, a text about who carries one, and the paiza artifact's own description.

label: Palace examination
summary: The game concept Palace Examination: the fourth and last of the imperial examinations, where the final entrants show their worth to the Son of Heaven at a palace feast.
details: In a text, `[palace_examination|E]` shows the words "Palace Examination" linked to the concept's explanation. Passing it gives a modifier. Vanilla uses it in merit rank texts, where officials of the highest ranks are expected to have passed it.

label: Palace examination icon
summary: The icon of the game concept Palace Examination (the last of the imperial examinations).
details: In a text, `[palace_examination_i|E]` is meant to show the palace exam icon linked to the concept's explanation. Its English text is `@palace_exam_icon` without the closing `!` that the other icon names have. No vanilla text uses this name.

label: Depose antipope
summary: The game concept Depose Antipope: a casus belli for Christian kings and above who neither back nor are a rival head of faith, against an independent ruler of their faith who backs one.
details: In a text, `[pam_antiking_cb|E]` shows the words "Depose Antipope" linked to the concept's explanation. The war deposes the rival head of faith and earns the gratitude of the rightful head of faith. Vanilla uses it in the rival head of faith concept text.

label: Challenge head of faith
summary: The game concept Challenge Head of Faith: a casus belli for a rival head of faith, or their backer, against the rightful head of their faith.
details: In a text, `[pam_challenge_hof_cb|E]` shows the words "Challenge Head of Faith" linked to the concept's explanation. Winning makes the challenger head of faith and their rite the mainline rite; a backer who wins and outranks the challenger also takes them as a vassal.

label: Guide the Christian Church
summary: The game concept Guide the Christian Church: a decision for prelates and mighty rulers that pushes the Christian Church towards the chapter they choose.
details: In a text, `[pam_shape_the_christian_church_decision|E]` shows the decision's name ("Guide the Christian Church") linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in a text where dynasty members can take it regardless of rank, with double impact.

label: Papabile score
summary: The game concept Papabile Score: each cardinal's score for papal elections, counting their traits, piety level, rite and the other cardinals' opinion of them.
details: In a text, `[papabile_score|E]` shows the words "Papabile Score" linked to the concept's explanation. Cardinals with the highest scores tend to get more votes; an interaction and a decision can raise it. Vanilla uses it in succession and antipope war texts.

label: Papabile scores
summary: Another name of the game concept Papabile Score, in the plural: the cardinals' scores for papal elections.
details: In a text, `[papabile_scores|E]` shows the words "Papabile Scores" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in the cardinals window.

label: Papal bull
summary: The game concept Papal Bull: a formal decree of a Christian head of faith, backed by the Christian Church.
details: In a text, `[papal_bull|E]` shows the words "Papal Bull" linked to the concept's explanation. A Christian head of faith with enough church authority issues one through a decision, spending piety, for example to call a great holy war or denounce a rite as heresy. Vanilla uses it in decision and catalyst texts.

label: Papal bulls
summary: Another name of the game concept Papal Bull, in the plural: formal decrees of a Christian head of faith.
details: In a text, `[papal_bulls|E]` shows the words "Papal Bulls" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in a Christian Church chapter text.

label: Favored candidate
summary: The game concept Favored Candidate: in a great holy war, the member of the attacking faith who already holds or claims the main target and so counts as its rightful receiver.
details: In a text, `[papal_recipient|E]` shows the words "Favored Candidate" linked to the concept's explanation. The main contributor can give precedence to their own beneficiary instead. Vanilla uses it in the great holy war window ("Override" or "Comply with").

label: Paper map
summary: The game concept Paper Map: the most zoomed-out map view, an overview of all independent realms in the world.
details: In a text, `[paper_zoom|E]` shows the words "Paper Map" linked to the concept's explanation, which is the map's own zoom-level tooltip. In this view, clicking the map selects realms. Vanilla uses it in a concept text listing the zoom levels.

label: Partition share
summary: The game concept Partition Share: under a succession law with several heirs, the titles one particular heir will inherit.
details: In a text, `[partition_share|E]` shows the words "Partition Share" linked to the concept's explanation. Usually the titles are split between a ruler's children, rarely their siblings, in a way that depends on the kind of succession. No vanilla text uses this name.

label: Patrilineal
summary: The game concept Patrilineal: a marriage in which the children are born into their father's house.
details: In a text, `[patrilineal|E]` shows the word "Patrilineal" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in the game rule texts on matrilineal marriages and in marriage condition texts.

label: Pax Romana casus belli
summary: The game concept Pax Romana Casus Belli: a strong reason for war that only the ruler of the Roman Empire has, to bring in a new Pax Romana.
details: In a text, `[pax_romana_invasion_casus_belli|E]` shows the words "Pax Romana Casus Belli" linked to the concept's explanation. It can target a whole empire title at once, for fast expansion. Vanilla uses it in the Roman restoration event that grants it.

label: Homage
summary: The game concept Homage: an activity in which vassals formally show their loyalty to their liege.
details: In a text, `[pay_homage|E]` shows the word "Homage" linked to the concept's explanation. Homage can be paid in several ways and can give opinion, prestige and dynasty prestige to both sides. Vanilla uses it in the pay homage decision texts.

label: Peace
summary: The game concept Peace: the end of a war, as a victory, a defeat or a white peace.
details: In a text, `[peace|E]` shows the word "Peace" linked to the concept's explanation. At 100% war score the other side cannot refuse a peace offer and must accept defeat; what victory or defeat means depends on the casus belli and war target. Vanilla uses it in peace acceptance texts.

label: Peace offer
summary: Another name of the game concept Peace, as "Peace Offer": a proposal to end a war as a victory, a defeat or a white peace.
details: In a text, `[peace_offer|E]` shows the words "Peace Offer" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in the war and war score concept texts.

label: Peace offers
summary: Another name of the game concept Peace, in the plural "Peace Offers": proposals to end a war.
details: In a text, `[peace_offers|E]` shows the words "Peace Offers" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in the victory, defeat and white peace concept texts.

label: Peasant faction
summary: The game concept Peasant Faction: a faction made of counties with low county opinion, which revolts even when its military power is low.
details: In a text, `[peasant_faction|E]` shows the words "Peasant Faction" linked to the concept's explanation. A successful peasant revolt lowers control in the realm a lot. Vanilla uses it in faction texts.

label: Peasant factions
summary: Another name of the game concept Peasant Faction, in the plural: factions of unhappy counties that revolt even when weak.
details: In a text, `[peasant_factions|E]` shows the words "Peasant Factions" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in tradition and decision texts.

label: Peasant militia
summary: The game concept Peasant Militia: men-at-arms armed with pitchforks and spears.
details: In a text, `[peasant_militia|E]` shows the words "Peasant Militia" linked to the concept's explanation. They usually counter heavy and light cavalry, are countered by heavy infantry, and are strong in mountains and fertile terrain. Vanilla uses it in regiment and modifier names.

label: Perk
summary: The game concept Perk: an unlockable bonus with useful effects, bought with a lifestyle's experience after choosing a focus in that lifestyle.
details: In a text, `[perk|E]` shows the word "Perk" linked to the concept's explanation. For example, intrigue experience unlocks intrigue lifestyle perks. Vanilla uses it in the texts of effects that grant perk points.

label: Perks
summary: Another name of the game concept Perk, in the plural: unlockable bonuses bought with lifestyle experience.
details: In a text, `[perks|E]` shows the word "Perks" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in the refund perks effect text and lifestyle texts.

label: Permit (tenet status)
summary: Another name of the game concept Permitted, as the verb "Permit": to give a core tenet the status where the rite approves of it without promoting it.
details: In a text, `[permit_tenet_status|E]` shows the word "Permit" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in a papal bull option ("Select a core tenet to permit within your faith").

label: Permitted (tenet status)
summary: The game concept Permitted: a tenet status meaning the rite approves of a core tenet or doctrine without actively promoting it.
details: In a text, `[permitted_tenet_status|E]` shows the word "Permitted" linked to the concept's explanation. A character of that rite can take such a tenet as a personal tenet with no spiritual penalty. Vanilla uses it in decision and trait weight texts.

label: Perpetual hook
summary: The game concept Perpetual Hook: a hook (a favor owed, or leverage) on a character that is not used up, but goes on cooldown after each use.
details: In a text, `[perpetual_hook|E]` shows the words "Perpetual Hook" linked to the concept's explanation. It cannot force someone to be your agent in a murder scheme and gives no passive bonus; for that a strong hook is needed. Vanilla uses it in the texts of the effect that adds a hook.

label: Perpetual hooks
summary: Another name of the game concept Perpetual Hook, in the plural: hooks on characters that are not used up but go on cooldown.
details: In a text, `[perpetual_hooks|E]` shows the words "Perpetual Hooks" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in a tenet text where parents get them on their children.

label: Iranian Intermezzo
summary: The game concept Iranian Intermezzo: the struggle that shows the troubled decline of the Abbasid Caliphate, with rebellions in Mesopotamia and Persian rulers breaking free.
details: In a text, `[persian_struggle|E]` shows the words "Iranian Intermezzo" linked to the concept's explanation. Characters involved mostly choose to be supporters, who work to restore the caliphate's power, or detractors. Vanilla also writes `persian_struggle.GetFullName` in rich presence status texts, where the same name is used for the struggle itself, not this concept.

label: Personal scheme
summary: Another name of the game concept Personal Scheme, as the word "Personal": schemes that aim to create a bond or status between the plotter and the target.
details: In a text, `[personal|E]` shows the word "Personal" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it when listing the scheme types and in a camp temperament text.

label: Personal artifact claim
summary: The game concept Personal Artifact Claim: a claim on an artifact that belongs to you personally, as opposed to one held by your house.
details: In a text, `[personal_artifact_claim|E]` shows the words "Personal Artifact Claim" linked to the concept's explanation. When you die, your children get claims on all your artifacts; you also get one when an artifact of yours is stolen in a siege or raid. Artifact claims are never inherited.

label: Personal artifact claims
summary: Another name of the game concept Personal Artifact Claim, in the plural: claims on artifacts that belong to a character personally.
details: In a text, `[personal_artifact_claims|E]` shows the words "Personal Artifact Claims" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in the interaction that buys claims with piety or prestige and in the artifact claim concept text.

label: Personal movement power
summary: The game concept Personal Movement Power: how much one member adds to the total power of their movement in the dynastic cycle.
details: In a text, `[personal_movement_power|E]` shows the words "Personal Movement Power" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in minister and diarchy texts.

label: Power (personal movement)
summary: Another name of the game concept Personal Movement Power, in a short form: how much one member adds to their movement's power.
details: In a text, `[personal_movement_power_short|E]` shows just the word "Power" linked to the Personal Movement Power explanation. Vanilla uses it in movement and disciple texts.

label: Personal obligations
summary: Another name of the game concept Secular Obligations, as "Personal Obligations": the rules for how much of the church holdings' income goes to the local secular ruler.
details: In a text, `[personal_obligations|E]` shows the words "Personal Obligations" linked to the concept's explanation. The concept text names personal and fixed secular obligations as the two types, set by the Christian Church's situation. No vanilla text uses this name.

label: Personal scheme
summary: The game concept Personal Scheme: a scheme that aims to create a bond or status between the plotter and the target, such as sway, befriend, seduce or elope.
details: In a text, `[personal_scheme|E]` shows the words "Personal Scheme" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in success chance texts.

label: Personal schemes
summary: Another name of the game concept Personal Scheme, in the plural: schemes that aim to create a bond or status between plotter and target.
details: In a text, `[personal_schemes|E]` shows the words "Personal Schemes" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in the intrigue window and the max personal schemes modifier.

label: Personal tenet
summary: The game concept Personal Tenet: a core tenet that a ruler takes on as a central part of their own faith.
details: In a text, `[personal_tenet|E]` shows the words "Personal Tenet" linked to the concept's explanation. Taking one that the faith holds as core or permitted gives spiritual fulfillment; a prohibited one becomes a secret. Personal tenets also give effects and unlock special mechanics.

label: Personal tenets
summary: Another name of the game concept Personal Tenet, in the plural: core tenets a ruler takes on as part of their own faith.
details: In a text, `[personal_tenets|E]` shows the words "Personal Tenets" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in important action and interaction texts.

label: Personalities
summary: Another name of the game concept Personality, in the plural: how characters behave, set mainly by their personality traits.
details: In a text, `[personalities|E]` shows the word "Personalities" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in the game rule texts on AI conquerors.

label: Personality
summary: The game concept Personality: how a character acts towards others, set mainly by their personality traits.
details: In a text, `[personality|E]` shows the word "Personality" linked to the concept's explanation. A ruler's behavior can also be changed by some modifiers and special traits such as Conqueror. Vanilla uses it in faction reason texts.

label: Personality icon
summary: The icon of the game concept Personality (how a character acts, set mainly by personality traits).
details: In a text, `[personality_i|E]` shows the personality icon linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla writes it without `|E` (`[personality_i]`) before a character's AI personality in a tooltip.

label: Personality trait
summary: The game concept Personality Trait: a trait that shapes a character's outlook and which actions they tend to take.
details: In a text, `[personality_trait|E]` shows "Personality Trait" linked to the concept's explanation. Personality traits also change how others feel about the character (opinion), can be gained and lost during a life, and acting against them causes stress. Vanilla uses it in decision and court position texts about gaining or losing such traits.

label: Personality trait
summary: The plural name of the game concept Personality Trait: traits that shape a character's outlook and which actions they tend to take.
details: In a text, `[personality_traits|E]` shows "Personality Traits" linked to the Personality Trait explanation. Vanilla uses it in concept texts about stress and in AI personality texts.

label: Petition antipope for gold
summary: The game concept Petition Antipope for Gold: an interaction with which a follower of a challenger head of faith asks their antipope for gold.
details: In a text, `[petition_antipope_gold_interaction|E]` shows "Petition Antipope for Gold" linked to the concept's explanation. Only characters following a challenger head of faith can use it; the concept text says their sponsor is accepted automatically. Vanilla lists it in the concept text about challenger heads of faith.

label: Seek antipope's indulgence
summary: The game concept Seek Antipope's Indulgence: an interaction with which a follower of a challenger head of faith pays their antipope gold for forgiveness and piety.
details: In a text, `[petition_antipope_indulgences_interaction|E]` shows "Seek Antipope's Indulgence" linked to the concept's explanation. It goes around the head of faith of the main rite; the concept text says their sponsor is accepted automatically. Vanilla lists it in the concept text about challenger heads of faith.

label: Petition
summary: The game concept Petition: a chance for vassals to ask their liege for help with an issue.
details: In a text, `[petition_liege|E]` shows "Petition" linked to the concept's explanation. Many kinds of issue can be raised, and the liege decides whether to grant it. Vanilla uses it in the petition decision; in the petition event texts `petition_liege` is also a saved scope (`[petition_liege.GetLadyLord]`), which is a different thing.

label: Physical trait
summary: The game concept Physical Trait: a trait about a character's body, looks or behaviour, or about how intelligent they are.
details: In a text, `[physical_trait|E]` shows "Physical Trait" linked to the concept's explanation. Many of these traits change how attractive others find the character, and they are often congenital (present from birth and permanent). Vanilla uses it as the name of the physical trait category.

label: Physical trait
summary: The plural name of the game concept Physical Trait: traits about a character's body, looks or behaviour, or about how intelligent they are.
details: In a text, `[physical_traits|E]` shows "Physical Traits" linked to the Physical Trait explanation. No vanilla text uses this name.

label: Piety
summary: The game concept Piety: how virtuous a character is, a resource gained by acting according to their faith.
details: In a text, `[piety|E]` shows "Piety" linked to the concept's explanation. Following the doctrines of one's faith, for example by going on a pilgrimage, raises it; it is spent on religious matters. Every gain also moves the character towards the next level of devotion. Vanilla uses it in hundreds of places in the game's texts and interface files.

label: Devotion
summary: The game concept Devotion: the points that move a character towards their next level of devotion.
details: In a text, `[piety_experience|E]` shows "Devotion" linked to the concept's explanation. A character gains as much devotion as the piety they gain. Vanilla uses it in effect texts that say how much devotion was gained or lost.

label: Piety
summary: The icon form of the game concept Piety: it shows the piety icon instead of a word.
details: The concept text for this name is the local player's piety icon. `[piety_i|E]` links the icon to the Piety explanation; vanilla often writes `[piety_i]` without `|E`, which shows only the icon in front of a value ("[piety_i] $VALUE$").

label: Level of devotion
summary: The game concept Level of Devotion: how devout and virtuous a character is seen to be, and their standing within their faith.
details: In a text, `[piety_level|E]` shows "Level of Devotion" linked to the concept's explanation. Gaining piety moves a character towards the next level; the concept text lists each level with its modifier. Vanilla uses it in achievement and building texts.

label: Level of devotion impact
summary: The game concept Level of Devotion Impact: makes the modifiers a character gets from their current level of devotion stronger or weaker.
details: In a text, `[piety_level_impact|E]` shows "Level of Devotion Impact" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in the name of the modifier that changes this impact.

label: Level of devotion
summary: The plural name of the game concept Level of Devotion: how devout and virtuous a character is seen to be.
details: In a text, `[piety_levels|E]` shows "Level(s) of Devotion" linked to the Level of Devotion explanation. Vanilla uses it in effect texts that say how many levels were gained or lost.

label: Pilgrimage
summary: The game concept Pilgrimage: an activity in which a character travels to a holy site of their faith.
details: In a text, `[pilgrimage|E]` shows "Pilgrimage" linked to the concept's explanation. Most faiths allow it; each holy site has a waiting time before it can be visited again. The journey can bring both chances and dangers, and arriving earns piety and sometimes other rewards.

label: Pilgrimage
summary: The plural name of the game concept Pilgrimage: activities in which characters travel to holy sites of their faith.
details: In a text, `[pilgrimages|E]` shows "Pilgrimages" linked to the Pilgrimage explanation. Vanilla uses it in achievement, legacy and law texts.

label: Piety
summary: The adjective form of the game concept Piety ("Pious"), linked to the Piety explanation.
details: In a text, `[pious|E]` shows "Pious" linked to the Piety explanation. Vanilla uses it in scheme and cultural tradition texts, for example that rulers with a certain trait are seen as pious.

label: Pious builder
summary: The icon form of the game concept Pious Builder, the AI personality that spends its gold on gaining piety.
details: The concept text for this name is the pious builder icon. Vanilla writes `[pious_builder_i]` without `|E`, which shows only the icon, in front of the personality's name. A pious builder pays for religious buildings, great projects, activities and decisions, and saves gold only when directly threatened.

label: Pious building
summary: The game concept Pious Building: a building whose main purpose is to raise the piety its holding gives.
details: In a text, `[pious_building|E]` shows "Pious Building" linked to the concept's explanation. No vanilla text uses this name.

label: Pious building
summary: The plural name of the game concept Pious Building: buildings whose main purpose is to raise the piety their holding gives.
details: In a text, `[pious_buildings|E]` shows "Pious Buildings" linked to the Pious Building explanation. Vanilla uses it in government and mandala texts about extra piety for building them.

label: Plague intensity
summary: The highest level of the game concept Plague Intensity ("Apocalyptic"), linked to the Plague Intensity explanation.
details: In a text, `[plague_apocalyptic|E]` shows "Apocalyptic" linked to the Plague Intensity explanation. An epidemic's intensity (apocalyptic, major or minor) decides how far it spreads, how long it lasts and whom it infects. Vanilla uses it as the name of the apocalyptic epidemic level.

label: Plague intensity
summary: The plural name of the game concept Plague Intensity: the levels (apocalyptic, major, minor) an epidemic can have.
details: In a text, `[plague_intensities|E]` shows "Plague Intensities" linked to the Plague Intensity explanation. Vanilla uses it in the epidemic concept text.

label: Plague intensity
summary: The game concept Plague Intensity: whether an epidemic is apocalyptic, major or minor.
details: In a text, `[plague_intensity|E]` shows "Plague Intensity" linked to the concept's explanation. The intensity decides how far the epidemic spreads, how long it lasts and which characters it infects and kills. No vanilla text uses this name.

label: Plague intensity
summary: The middle level of the game concept Plague Intensity ("Major"), linked to the Plague Intensity explanation.
details: In a text, `[plague_major|E]` shows "Major" linked to the Plague Intensity explanation. Vanilla uses it as the name of the major epidemic level and in situation catalyst texts.

label: Plague intensity
summary: The lowest level of the game concept Plague Intensity ("Minor"), linked to the Plague Intensity explanation.
details: In a text, `[plague_minor|E]` shows "Minor" linked to the Plague Intensity explanation. Vanilla uses it as the name of the minor epidemic level.

label: Player heir
summary: The game concept Player Heir: the heir a player goes on playing as when their character dies.
details: In a text, `[player_heir|E]` shows "Player Heir" linked to the concept's explanation. Usually this is the primary heir; when the primary title's succession law would pass it outside the player's dynasty, the player instead continues as the dynasty's heir to their next highest title. With no player heir the game ends.

label: Point of interest
summary: The game concept Point of Interest: a place in the world worth visiting, which gives its benefits on the first visit.
details: In a text, `[point_of_interest|E]` shows "Point of Interest" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in perk effect texts about rewards for visiting such places.

label: Point of interest
summary: The plural name of the game concept Point of Interest: places in the world worth visiting, which give benefits on the first visit.
details: In a text, `[points_of_interest|E]` shows "Points of Interest" linked to the Point of Interest explanation. Vanilla uses it in decision texts about maps and in the wanderer lifestyle text.

label: Political scheme
summary: The short name of the game concept Political Scheme ("Political"), linked to the Political Scheme explanation.
details: In a text, `[political|E]` shows "Political" linked to the Political Scheme explanation. Vanilla uses it where scheme types are listed (personal, hostile, political, contract).

label: Political scheme
summary: The game concept Political Scheme: the kind of scheme of a political and bureaucratic nature, used by administrative governments.
details: In a text, `[political_scheme|E]` shows "Political Scheme" linked to the concept's explanation. The concept text lists them: Challenge Status, Depose, Expand Power Base, Generate Claim, Promote and Slander; with the All Under Heaven DLC it also lists the mandala government's schemes, such as Coerce Tributary.

label: Political scheme
summary: The plural name of the game concept Political Scheme: schemes of a political and bureaucratic nature, used by administrative governments.
details: In a text, `[political_schemes|E]` shows "Political Schemes" linked to the Political Scheme explanation. Vanilla uses it in texts about success chance against such schemes.

label: Political map
summary: The game concept Political Map: the map mode that gives an overview of the rulers in an area.
details: In a text, `[political_zoom|E]` shows "Political Map" linked to the concept's explanation. It is meant for planning wars, managing vassals and exploring realms; in this map mode a click on the map selects a realm. Vanilla uses it in the concept text about the map's zoom levels.

label: Populist faction
summary: The game concept Populist Faction: a faction of unhappy counties sharing a culture or faith that want to break away under a new ruler.
details: In a text, `[popular_faction|E]` shows "Populist Faction" linked to the concept's explanation. Its members are counties with low county opinion (how the people of a county feel about their ruler); they pick a new ruler of their culture or faith. The game calls such uprisings very dangerous.

label: Populist faction
summary: The plural name of the game concept Populist Faction: factions of unhappy counties that want to break away under a new ruler of their culture or faith.
details: In a text, `[popular_factions|E]` shows "Populist Factions" linked to the Populist Faction explanation. Vanilla uses it in cultural tradition and situation texts that make such factions more or less common.

label: Power sharing
summary: The game concept Power Sharing: a ruler shares some authority with a vassal or courtier, who becomes their diarch.
details: In a text, `[power_sharing|E]` shows "Power Sharing" linked to the concept's explanation. The ruler can give the diarch mandates, and the diarch can use special diarch powers; the scales of power show which of the two holds more authority. Vanilla uses it in texts about diarchy types.

label: Powerful family
summary: The short name of the game concept Powerful Family ("Powerful"), linked to the Powerful Family explanation.
details: In a text, `[powerful|E]` shows "Powerful" linked to the Powerful Family explanation. Vanilla uses it in faction texts, for example that a claimant's noble family is powerful.

label: Powerful family
summary: The plural name of the game concept Powerful Family: the most influential houses of an administrative realm.
details: In a text, `[powerful_families|E]` shows "Powerful Families" linked to the Powerful Family explanation. Vanilla uses it in law texts and in an interaction text about co-emperors.

label: Powerful family
summary: The game concept Powerful Family: one of the most influential houses and noble families of an administrative realm.
details: In a text, `[powerful_family|E]` shows "Powerful Family" linked to the concept's explanation. Members of a powerful family do better at political schemes and get their way more often in interactions. Only a limited number of families count as powerful at a time: those with the highest rating.

label: Powerful family attribute
summary: The game concept Powerful Family Attribute: a set of bonuses tied to a house in an administrative realm, for its members and their liege.
details: In a text, `[powerful_family_attribute|E]` shows "Powerful Family Attribute" linked to the concept's explanation. The bonuses work only while the house counts as a powerful family; a dominant family's attribute does not help the liege. The house head can change the attribute at any time.

label: Powerful family rating
summary: The game concept Powerful Family Rating: a measure of how influential a powerful family is.
details: In a text, `[powerful_family_rating|E]` shows "Powerful Family Rating" linked to the concept's explanation. The number of governorships the house holds matters most. A house needs a minimum rating (a define, `NHouse` `POWERFUL_HOUSE_MINIMUM_POWER`) to count as powerful.

label: Powerful family rating
summary: A shorter name of the game concept Powerful Family Rating ("Family Rating"), linked to its explanation.
details: In a text, `[powerful_family_rating_mid|E]` shows "Family Rating" linked to the Powerful Family Rating explanation. Vanilla uses it in AI interaction reasons that compare two families' ratings.

label: Powerful family rating
summary: The shortest name of the game concept Powerful Family Rating ("Rating"), linked to its explanation.
details: In a text, `[powerful_family_rating_short|E]` shows "Rating" linked to the Powerful Family Rating explanation. Vanilla uses it in a concept text about powerful houses.

label: Powerful vassal
summary: The game concept Powerful Vassal: one of the few vassals with the most soldiers and the highest income.
details: In a text, `[powerful_vassal|E]` shows "Powerful Vassal" linked to the concept's explanation. Powerful vassals expect a council seat and like their liege much less without one. Changing a succession law needs every powerful vassal to have a positive opinion of the liege, be cowed by them, or be imprisoned.

label: Powerful vassal
summary: The possessive form of the game concept Powerful Vassal ("Powerful Vassal's"), linked to its explanation.
details: In a text, `[powerful_vassal_possessive|E]` shows "Powerful Vassal's" linked to the Powerful Vassal explanation. Vanilla uses it once, in a struggle text about removing a vassal's religious protection.

label: Powerful vassal
summary: The adjective form of the game concept Powerful Vassal ("Powerful"), linked to the Powerful Vassal explanation.
details: In a text, `[powerful_vassal_powerful|E]` shows "Powerful" linked to the Powerful Vassal explanation. Vanilla uses it once, in a succession text ("Be a powerful de jure vassal").

label: Powerful vassal
summary: The plural name of the game concept Powerful Vassal: the few vassals with the most soldiers and the highest income.
details: In a text, `[powerful_vassals|E]` shows "Powerful Vassals" linked to the Powerful Vassal explanation. Vanilla uses it in achievement, law and succession texts.

label: Predicted scheme difficulty
summary: A shorter name of the game concept Predicted Scheme Difficulty ("Predicted Difficulty"), linked to its explanation.
details: In a text, `[predicted_difficulty|E]` shows "Predicted Difficulty" linked to the Predicted Scheme Difficulty explanation. Vanilla uses it in the interaction window next to the predicted odds level of a scheme.

label: Predicted scheme difficulty
summary: The game concept Predicted Scheme Difficulty: an estimate, before a scheme starts, of how hard it will be.
details: In a text, `[predicted_scheme_difficulty|E]` shows "Predicted Scheme Difficulty" linked to the concept's explanation. Some factors are only known once the scheme begins and agents join, so it is only a prediction; the concept text names five levels, from likely easy, fast and silent down to costly. No vanilla text uses this name.

label: Vassal stance
summary: A name of the game concept Vassal Stance ("Preferred Heir"): each vassal's stance decides which heir they would like to succeed.
details: In a text, `[preferred_heir|E]` shows "Preferred Heir" linked to the Vassal Stance explanation. A vassal's stance also shapes their opinion of the liege; vassals of the same stance like and dislike the same things. Vanilla uses it in faction reasons such as the liege having been the preferred heir.

label: Vassal stance
summary: A plural name of the game concept Vassal Stance ("Preferred Heirs"), linked to the Vassal Stance explanation.
details: In a text, `[preferred_heirs|E]` shows "Preferred Heirs" linked to the Vassal Stance explanation. Each vassal stance prefers one heir. No vanilla text uses this name.

label: Preparation phase
summary: The game concept Preparation Phase: the time before an undirected great holy war is declared.
details: In a text, `[preparation_phase|E]` shows "Preparation Phase" linked to the concept's explanation. Rulers of the attacking faith can pledge troops or give to the war chest, and defenders can pledge against it; when the timer runs out the war is declared. Vanilla uses it in the decision that starts such a war.

label: Pressed claim
summary: The adjective form of the game concept Pressed Claim ("Pressed"), linked to the Pressed Claim explanation.
details: In a text, `[pressed|E]` shows "Pressed" linked to the Pressed Claim explanation. Vanilla uses it in effect texts such as a claim becoming pressed.

label: Pressed claim
summary: The game concept Pressed Claim: a claim on a title that counts as legally strong.
details: In a text, `[pressed_claim|E]` shows "Pressed Claim" linked to the concept's explanation. The claimant's children inherit it, but only as unpressed claims. Vanilla uses it in effect texts such as gaining a pressed claim on a title.

label: Pressed claim
summary: The icon form of the game concept Pressed Claim: it shows the pressed claim icon instead of a word.
details: The concept text for this name is the pressed claim icon. Vanilla writes `[pressed_claim_i]` without `|E`, which shows only the icon, in front of scheme agent texts about claimed counties.

label: Pressed claim
summary: The plural name of the game concept Pressed Claim: claims on titles that count as legally strong.
details: In a text, `[pressed_claims|E]` shows "Pressed Claims" linked to the Pressed Claim explanation. Vanilla uses it in texts about claims turning pressed.

label: Prestige
summary: The game concept Prestige: a character's fame and social standing, a resource spent on worldly matters.
details: In a text, `[prestige|E]` shows "Prestige" linked to the concept's explanation. What it can be spent on depends on the government form, doctrines and more. Every gain also moves the character towards the next level of fame. Vanilla uses it in hundreds of places in the game's texts and interface files.

label: Fame
summary: The game concept Fame: the points that move a character towards their next level of fame.
details: In a text, `[prestige_experience|E]` shows "Fame" linked to the concept's explanation. A character gains as much fame as the prestige they gain. Vanilla uses it in effect texts that say how much fame was gained or lost.

label: Fame
summary: The icon form of the game concept Fame: it shows the prestige icon, linked to the Fame explanation.
details: The concept text for this name is the same as `prestige_i`'s, the prestige icon. Vanilla writes `[prestige_experience_i|E]` in front of the word, as in "[prestige_experience_i|E][prestige_experience|E]" in perk texts.

label: Prestige
summary: The icon form of the game concept Prestige: it shows the prestige icon instead of a word.
details: The concept text for this name is the prestige icon. `[prestige_i|E]` links the icon to the Prestige explanation; written without `|E` it shows only the icon, usually in front of a value. Vanilla uses it in hundreds of places in the game's texts and interface files.

label: Level of fame
summary: The game concept Level of Fame: a character's general reputation and how well everyone thinks of them.
details: In a text, `[prestige_level|E]` shows "Level of Fame" linked to the concept's explanation. Gaining prestige moves a character towards the next level; the concept text lists each level with its modifier. Vanilla uses it in achievement and other texts.
